_meta.name: English
_meta.note: The command line tool exists only in English by decision. The file exists anyway so that no user-facing text lives as a literal in code, and so every string can be reviewed in one place against part 5 of the glossary.

cli.usage:
Usage:
  bws list [--query TEXT] [--json] [--timing]
  bws stop|start|restart NAME [--dry-run] [--dependents] [--timeout SECONDS] [--json]
cli.optionNotForCommand: {0} does not apply to {1}. It works with: {2}.
cli.missingServiceName: {0} needs the name of a service. Example: bws {0} Spooler --dry-run
cli.badTimeout: --timeout takes a whole number of seconds, at least 1. It got: {0}
cli.plan.warning.cascade.one: Stopping {0} also stops one other entry: {2}
cli.plan.warning.inTheWay.one: One running entry needs {0} and is not included: {2}. The stop will be refused while it runs. Add --dependents to take it down too.
cli.plan.warning.inTheWay.many: {1} running entries need {0} and are not included: {2}. The stop will be refused while they run. Add --dependents to take them down too.
cli.plan.warning.sharedProcess: {0} shares its process with: {1}. Those keep running and the process does not go away.
cli.plan.warning.returnsAfterReboot: {0} starts automatically, so this lasts until the next restart of the machine.
cli.plan.warning.cascadeUnreadable: Could not read what depends on {0}, so more may stop than this plan shows.
cli.plan.warning.alreadyThere: {0} is already in that state, so nothing would change.
cli.run.interrupted: Interrupted. Finishing the step in flight, then putting back what was taken down. Another Ctrl+C leaves it as it is.
cli.run.abandoned: Leaving the rest undone. The report still follows, so you can see what was changed. Another Ctrl+C ends this without it.
cli.run.wasInterrupted: This run was interrupted. Steps that were never attempted say so above.
cli.run.outcome.earlierStepFailed: not tried, an earlier step did not work
cli.run.outcome.cancelled: not tried, the run was interrupted
cli.plan.problem.notOperable: {0} is a driver. This tool shows drivers but does not start or stop them.
cli.plan.problem.cascadeNotOperable: Stopping {0} would mean stopping these drivers first: {1}. This tool does not start or stop drivers, so there is no plan it can offer.
cli.plan.problem.cannotComeBack.target: {0} is disabled, so restarting it would stop it and could not start it again. Set it to start automatically or on demand first, or use bws stop if stopping it is what you want.
cli.plan.problem.cannotComeBack.one: {2} is disabled and restarting {0} would stop it, so it could not be started again. Set it to start automatically or on demand first, or use bws stop if stopping is what you want.
cli.plan.problem.cannotComeBack.many: {1} entries this restart would stop are disabled, so it could not start them again: {2}. Set them to start automatically or on demand first, or use bws stop if stopping them is what you want.
